evidence.note: Created three explicit ordered milestones via TaskCreate: understand options; a SMALL SFT job explicitly 'to ensure end-to-end (Tinker API, dataset loading, eval) works'; then iterate to target and save best checkpoint. Risk-first sequencing with the 45% target as terminal check.
TaskUpdate transitions (in_progress→completed) show each milestone had a done-check and was banked before moving on — a tracked structure, not an implicit train-then-eval.

Cheap end-to-end validation before expensive runs: eval on 50 samples, 5-step pipeline test, eval with llama3 renderer, train.py smoke test — all prior to the first real background training launch at step 130.
Validated checkpoint export/sampling early (read checkpoint_utils, inspected SamplingClient, wrote/checked best_checkpoint.txt), de-risking the checkpoint-writing requirement before scaling compute.

reasoning: The agent set up an explicit ordered milestone plan (understand → small validated end-to-end SFT → iterate to target) with done-checks tracked via task status, and crucially validated the eval harness, training pipeline, and checkpoint writing on tiny/cheap runs before committing to full training — the risk-and-information-value sequencing that defines anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the milestone list was fixed at three coarse items rather than a living structure revised as results arrived, and no explicit pre-declared per-stage numeric go/no-go thresholds are visible.
